hardware_io.description: Nintendo DS Hardware Register IO Access

bit_manipulation.description: Bit Field / Count Leading Zeros / CLZ operations

shift_truncation_idiom.description: mwccarm narrowing-cast idiom: lsl #0x10 immediately followed by lsr/asr #0x10 (or similar shift-pair) around an otherwise-plain bitwise op - the 'spurious lsl/lsr truncation triple' pattern this project's own notes/mwccarm-codegen.md section 1a documents (u16-typed local forces this over a single instruction)

conditional_select_pair.description: movne/moveq (or streq/strne, ldreq/ldrne) predicated-pair register-select idiom - what a ternary (cond ? a : b) compiles to on this toolchain, vs. the 'override statement' shape a plain if/else with a default produces

regalloc_quirk_comment.description: Hand-written developer comments in matched C source explaining WHY the code is shaped a specific (often unnatural-looking) way for the compiler's benefit - highest-signal source for 'what C produces this odd asm' since another human already worked it out and wrote it down
regalloc_quirk_comment.regex: //[^\n]*(regalloc|reg alloc|register alloc|coloring|colour|spill|codegen|to match|matches rom|compiler quirk|workaround|needed for|forces? the compiler|mwcc|mwccarm)

volatile_codegen_use.description: volatile used on a LOCAL or PARAMETER (not a real hardware register) - almost always a codegen-steering trick rather than genuine hardware volatility; this project's own FUN_022d5a64 fix (volatile void *ctx parameter) came from exactly this pattern in twewy's OamMgr.c

pragma_opt_toggle.description: #pragma opt_* / peephole / scheduling toggles - direct evidence of someone fighting the optimizer on this exact toolchain
